# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** 45  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)</sub>
- **Origin:** East Grafton  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>; Mrs.  <sub>[v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a little lady with snow-white, thick, wavy hair carefully arranged in becoming puffs and coils. Beneath her hair is an almost girlish face with pink cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and big, soft brown eyes. She favors dainty gowns, frills, and laces that suit her youthful charm.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c27 P22](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0022)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is imaginative, romantic, and retains a youthful freshness in her heart and soul. She delights in playfulness, pretending, and hosting imaginative tea parties. Although sweet-natured and happy, she admits to having been vain, coquettish, proud, and sulky during her youth.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)_

## Goals

- reunite and marry her true love Stephen Irving  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a quiet life at Echo Lodge in Grafton. In her youth, she was engaged to Stephen Irving, but after a silly quarrel fueled by pride on both sides, he left for the States, breaking her heart. Ten years prior to meeting Anne Shirley, her mother passed away, leading her to hire a series of young girls named Charlotta to keep her company, ending with Charlotta the Fourth. She befriended Anne Shirley and Diana Barry when they visited Echo Lodge, finding a kindred spirit in Anne. Through Anne's connection with Stephen's son Paul, Stephen Irving learned she was unmarried and returned to reconcile with her. The two were married in the honeysuckle arbor at Echo Lodge and subsequently relocated to Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c29 P5](../source/v02-c29.md#nw-v02-c29-p0005), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048)_

## Background by volume

- named Lavendar by her father because he loved the scent  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- hired little Charlotta Bowman for board and clothes ten years prior after her mother died  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- quarreled with Stephen Irving twenty-five years ago and remained unmarried  <sub>[v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- lived at Echo Lodge before her marriage  <sub>[v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v3 c7 P58](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0058)</sub>

## Quotes

> But what is the use of being an independent old maid if you can’t be silly when you want to, and when it doesn’t hurt anybody?  <sub>[v2 c21 P57](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0057)</sub>

> I knew I would rather be an old maid for a thousand years than marry anybody who wasn’t Stephen Irving.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> I’m really a very happy, contented little person in spite of my broken heart.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

> Oh, sometimes, I think it is of no use to make friends. They only go out of your life after awhile and leave a hurt that is worse than the emptiness before they came.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

> Anne, are you and Gilbert Blythe as good friends as you used to be?  <sub>[v3 c23 P22](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0022)</sub>
